name: Portugal
tagline: Europe's western edge, facing an ocean it once mapped, with the oldest fixed borders on the continent.
summary: Portugal has looked outward for six hundred years and inward for the rest, which shows in its architecture — Manueline stonework covered in ropes and sea creatures — and its food, built on cod fished off Newfoundland. The Atlantic keeps it cooler and wilder than Spain. Lisbon and Porto have both been thoroughly discovered; the Alentejo, the Beiras and the interior have not.

season.note: Spring and autumn are the best of it; the Algarve is full from June to September and the interior is very hot. The Douro harvest in late September is the country at its most itself. Winter is mild, wet and cheap.

getting_around: Alfa Pendular trains link Lisbon and Porto in under three hours. The Douro line is one of Europe's great scenic railways. Buses reach the Alentejo; a car helps everywhere rural.
food: Bacalhau, salt cod, in a claimed 365 preparations
Pastel de nata, eaten warm with cinnamon, standing at a counter
Grilled sardines in June, and the whole country smells of them

festivals.name: Santos Populares — sardines, basil and street parties
Festa de São João, with hammers and bonfires

know: The couvert — bread, olives, cheese put on your table — is charged unless you send it back.
Fado has two schools, Lisbon's and Coimbra's, and neither is background music.
Atlantic beaches have real currents; the flag system is enforced and worth obeying.

regions.name: Lisbon & the West
regions.summary: The capital on seven hills, a romantic mountain town above it, and the surf coast beyond.

cities.name: Lisbon
cities.summary: A tiled, hilly, sea-facing capital rebuilt on a grid after the 1755 earthquake, with trams that still climb the old parts.
highlights: The Gulbenkian, one of the best private collections ever assembled, in a garden
Jerónimos monastery's Manueline cloister at Belém
Tram 28 at seven in the morning, or not at all
Fado in Alfama, in a room of thirty people

experiences.name: Fado in a small house
experiences.summary: Lights down, conversation stops, and two guitars. The venues that ask for silence are the ones worth finding.

experiences.name: Azulejos, street by street
experiences.summary: Tiled facades were cheap weatherproofing before they were beautiful; the Tile Museum explains it and then the streets deliver it.

cities.name: Sintra
cities.summary: A microclimate of mist and forest on a ridge, with romantic palaces built into it by people with too much money.
highlights: Pena Palace, painted in colours that should not work
Quinta da Regaleira's initiation well, a spiral into the ground
The Moorish castle walls along the ridge

regions.name: Porto & the Douro
regions.summary: A granite river city, and the terraced valley that invented demarcated wine.

cities.name: Porto
cities.summary: Steep, granite and blue-tiled, with port lodges across the river and an ocean at the end of the tram line.
highlights: Livraria Lello, and the queue that proves it
Port lodges in Vila Nova de Gaia, tasted in order
São Bento station's 20,000 tiles
Francesinha, which is not for the faint-hearted

experiences.name: Port, tasted in the right order
experiences.summary: White, then tawny by age, then vintage — the tawnies are where the interest is and where the guides usually rush.

cities.name: Pinhão & the Douro valley
cities.summary: Terraced schist vineyards falling into a dammed river, worked by hand because machines cannot stand up on them.
highlights: The Douro railway along the water from Peso da Régua
Quintas that take guests and let you pick during harvest
Foot-treading in granite lagares, still done for the top wines

experiences.name: Treading grapes at harvest
experiences.summary: Knee-deep in a granite tank for two hours, in a line, to a rhythm — the least romantic and most enjoyable part of winemaking.

regions.name: The Alentejo & the South
regions.summary: Cork oak plains, a walled Roman city, and a wilder coast west of the Algarve.

cities.name: Évora
cities.summary: A walled town with a Roman temple in the middle, a chapel of bones, and megaliths in the fields around it.
highlights: The Temple of Diana, standing since the 1st century
The Capela dos Ossos and its unambiguous doorway inscription
Almendres cromlech, older than Stonehenge, and usually empty

experiences.name: Cork oaks and Alentejo reds
experiences.summary: The trees are stripped every nine years and the date is painted on the trunk; the wine estates between them charge a fraction of the Douro.

cities.name: Lagos & the Algarve
cities.summary: Golden cliffs, sea caves and the harbour that launched the age of exploration — and, less proudly, Europe's first slave market.
highlights: Ponta da Piedade's arches and grottoes by kayak
The Rota Vicentina north into the wild west coast
Cataplana seafood, cooked in its own copper pot
